Alpha 1.0.33 (magic at a glance)

  • Tap to understand your effects: Phones now have an Effects button beside the minimap. Open it to read buff and debuff names, descriptions and remaining time without needing mouse hover.
  • Keep your place: Long effect lists scroll independently, and countdown updates preserve your reading position. Expired effects disappear with a clear empty state when none remain.
  • Stay in control: Movement, Attack and skill buttons stay reachable while reading. Close or Escape dismisses the panel; opening chat or the phone menu also clears it without hiding chat.
  • Room on shorter screens: The minimap becomes compact on short landscape phones so it no longer overlaps Attack. Desktop effect icons remain unchanged. Wider camera, town-menu and physical-phone playability work continues.

Alpha 1.0.32 (time on your side)

  • Wards that last: Arcane Stability now extends Arcane Shield by 5% per rank. Five ranks increase its normal duration from 20 to 25 seconds, or its Extended rune duration from 30 to 37.5 seconds. Shield absorption is unchanged.
  • Control worth training: Prismatic Control now extends timed Wizard buffs and debuffs by 4% per rank: Spell Focus, Arcane Shield, Time Warp, Gravity Well's root and slow, Flame Whip's stun, Scorch Beam's armor reduction and Teleport's Phase protection. Projectile and ground-zone lifetimes are unchanged.
  • One clock for your magic: Duration bonuses combine at cast time after rune adjustments. Time Warp allies share the caster's improved duration; changing talents later does not rewrite an active effect. The server's remaining time drives buff timers and effect expiry.
  • Know your training: Arcane Stability and Prismatic Control descriptions now explain these duration benefits. Cooldowns, movement locks, saved ranks and other classes are unchanged; remaining range, area and talent effects are still under review.
  • General training stays within reach: Phone talent menus keep all general talents available after choosing a specialization. Each class still shows its active branch's skill talents alongside the general training, with deliberate purchases and saved ranks.

Alpha 1.0.31 (mercy in every pulse)

  • Healing training takes effect: Healing Light, Guardian Embrace and Divine Intervention Mastery now increase their actual multiplayer healing. Mercy Routine and Mercy Doctrine also improve spell healing, combining with equipment bonuses.
  • Every pulse counts once: Healing bonuses reach Guardian Embrace ticks, Consecrated Ground and the Spirit Guardians healing set bonus. Healing Light's Renewal rune keeps its cast-time strength without applying the same bonus twice; Beacon and Mass Revival share the improved heal.
  • Support your allies: The Spirit Guardians healing set bonus no longer restores health to opposing flagged PvP players. It still requires the set bonus and does not add free healing to the base ability.
  • Clearer training and feedback: Healing Mastery descriptions identify healing, and Mercy Doctrine no longer claims a Wisdom increase. Poison's healing penalty and overheal limits still apply; floating healing numbers report health actually restored. Duration, range and other outstanding talent effects remain under review.

Alpha 1.0.30 (a steadier hunt)

  • No stumble at the end of a wander: Fixed an Imp movement error that could interrupt game-loop updates when it reached a nearby roaming destination.
  • One source for enemy movement: Multiplayer Imps retain their server-directed movement and animation instead of starting a second local chase or wander. Local encounters still support normal roaming and pursuit.
  • Your journey stays yours: Quest requirements, rewards, enemy strength and saved progress are unchanged. Earlier patch notes remain available below.

Alpha 1.0.29 (make your training count)

  • Technique improves your uptime: Skill cooldown talents now affect real casts for all four classes. Skill-specific reductions combine with each other, then apply alongside your global cooldown reduction.
  • Spend less mana: Battle Breathing, Efficient Casting, Efficient Rites and Wizard Technique mana bonuses now reduce the server's spell cost. Equipment discounts retain their existing rounding before talent discounts apply.
  • Cast what you can afford: Desktop and phone input checks, predicted cooldowns and the primary ability's mana label use the same talent rules. A spell is no longer blocked locally when you have enough mana for its discounted cost.
  • Training survives the journey: Teleport charge recovery respects skill cooldown talents too. Wizard Technique, Lightstep and Cleanse Discipline descriptions identify their actual bonuses; existing ranks and earlier patch notes are retained.

Alpha 1.0.28 (every item in its place)

  • Loose gems belong in your bag: Clicking or dragging a gem no longer equips it into an invisible slot. Equipment actions now validate real character slots on both client and server; gems socketed through the Forge still work.
  • Recover misplaced items: If an older save contains an item in an unsupported equipment slot, open your bag's Recover stored items section. These items remain saved but grant no bonuses until used appropriately.
  • No partial recovery: Returning an item requires enough bag space for its full stack. A failed attempt leaves both the stored item and bag unchanged; freeing space lets you try again without losing or duplicating items.
  • Safe on desktop and phone: Recovery uses explicit, readable actions, validates the selected item, and saves successful returns. Normal equipment, socketed gems, quest-item protection, and earlier patch notes are preserved.

Alpha 1.0.27 (before the descent)

  • Ilyra helps you prepare: The first dungeon conversation explains the level-30 requirement and points you toward Earth exploration, earned equipment, and available skill and talent points before entering the Bastion.
  • Know the next realm's requirement: The four elemental dungeon objectives now show their actual entry levels in the Chronicle, journal, and quest tracker. Accepting a chapter does not bypass dungeon entry requirements.
  • Contracts remain your choice: Daily hunts are optional sources of gold and experience, not new prerequisites for the story. Dungeon objectives, manual turn-ins, rewards, and saved quest progress are unchanged.
  • Accurate town guidance: The town tracker and Help guide correctly name Verdant Bastion as the dungeon opened at level 30 and point you to the guide for later realms. The wider first-hour leveling journey remains under review.

Alpha 1.0.26 (know when you are ready)

  • A clearer dungeon invitation: the guide now shows the selected dungeon's real entry requirement and your current level. Verdant opens at 30, Abyssal at 60, Molten and Tempest at 70; the Dark Realm keeps its level and story gates.
  • No dead-end Start button: entry stays disabled while your level, run level, difficulty, or party-leader requirement is unmet. New adventurers no longer see a menu full of run levels they cannot enter.
  • The reason stays in reach: phone players see the unmet requirement beside the entry action, and changing dungeon updates the explanation immediately. Qualified party members can still continue their existing run.
  • Preparation still matters: this patch clarifies existing requirements; it does not lower dungeon gates, grant quest progress, or change XP rewards. The journey from Ilyra's early quests to the first dungeon remains under progression review.

Alpha 1.0.25 (a first step beyond the wards)

  • A gentler first encounter: Skeletons near Lanternhold now begin at level one and grow stronger farther from the town's wards, reaching the existing level-ten strength in the outer reaches. Elite Skeletons keep their strength but spawn beyond the starter band.
  • Follow Ilyra's directions: The opening Chronicle points you beyond the east gate, where three ordinary Skeleton encounters give new adventurers a reliable place to begin. They use normal combat, loot, quest credit and respawns.
  • Recall means return: Recalling to town clears the previous combat pursuit, queued abilities and movement input immediately, including when you were already in the overworld. An old target can no longer pull you away from your arrival point.
  • The wider adventure stays dangerous: Other enemy families, level-ten-and-higher profiles and dungeon scaling are unchanged. This starting-area correction does not change saved character stats, grant quest completion or bypass dungeon and raid requirements.

Alpha 1.0.24 (room for the adventure)

  • Less clutter over the world: Phone Bag, Hero, Quests, World Map and Social shortcuts now live behind one labeled Menu button. Health and resource numbers are larger, and the crowded short-landscape top bar no longer overlaps them.
  • A menu made for touch: Navigation uses readable, spaced controls in a scrolling panel. Back to game stays reachable above the scrolling actions, and chat remains visible below.
  • One destination at a time: Choosing an adventure menu closes the navigation panel first. Opening chat closes the panel, and opening Menu releases held movement input. Camera zoom and desktop navigation are unchanged.
  • More room, still more to do: Portrait objectives move into the space freed by the old shortcut row. Physical-phone verification, party-target ergonomics and the remaining menu redesign are still part of the wider mobile roadmap.
